questions.understand_first: This question is about a threshold and what happens when people disagree about whether it was crossed. Port State control is an intrusion on a foreign flag ship, so the Procedures constrain it: without clear grounds, the officer may look at the certificates and form a general impression, and that is all. Clear grounds is the key that unlocks the more detailed inspection, and from that inspection a detention may follow. So when a Chief Engineer disputes a detention, the dispute is almost always really about one of two things — whether the grounds were clear, or whether the deficiency found is genuinely detainable. And here is the part candidates get wrong: the system gives you a right of appeal but no stay. The ship does not sail while you argue. That single fact determines the whole of the correct behaviour in limbs (b) and (c) — you work the deficiency and build the record at the same time, because the fastest route to sea is rectification, and the record is what wins the review afterwards.

steps.title: Clear grounds - the definition, and why the term matters
points: A.1185(33) paragraph 1.7.2 - evidence that the ship, its equipment or its crew do not correspond substantially with the requirements of the relevant conventions
or that the master or crew members are not familiar with essential shipboard procedures relating to the safety of ships or the prevention of pollution
paragraph 2.4.1 supplies the force of the term - WITHOUT clear grounds the inspection is limited to valid certificates and documentation plus an overall impression
so clear grounds are not needed to board; they are needed to go further than the paperwork
paragraph 2.5.1 - clear grounds, or the absence of valid certificates, trigger the more detailed inspection
it is an evidence standard, not a suspicion - the PSCO must be able to point at something

steps.title: The circumstances that establish clear grounds
points: paragraph 2.4.2 lists nine, and says expressly that they include but are not limited to
absence of principal equipment or arrangements required by the conventions
evidence from a review of the certificates that a certificate is invalid
required certificates or documents not on board, incomplete, not maintained or falsely maintained
serious hull or structural deterioration risking structural, watertight or weathertight integrity
serious deficiencies in safety, pollution prevention or navigational equipment
master or crew not familiar with essential shipboard operations, or those operations not carried out
key crew members unable to communicate with each other or with others on board
false distress alerts not followed by proper cancellation
a report or complaint that the ship appears to be substandard

steps.title: Immediate actions on board - what a Chief Engineer does in the first hours
points: cooperate fully; a detention is not suspended by argument and obstruction converts a technical dispute into a conduct problem
attend the closing meeting with the master and ask the PSCO to identify, for each deficiency, the CONVENTION REFERENCE and the detainable ground relied on
obtain the inspection report - Form A and Form B - and check every entry against the machinery, the certificates and the records
sign as acknowledging receipt, not as agreeing; record disagreement in writing on the face of the report where the form allows
assemble the counter-evidence at once - certificates, survey reports, PMS records, alarm and test logs, spare-part records, photographs, parameter printouts
check paragraph 1.2.6 - an Exemption Certificate correctly referenced, or approved alternative design and arrangements documentation, means the ship is to be interpreted as complying
notify the Company and the DPA immediately; the company, not the ship, is the party with the right of appeal
raise it in the SMS as a non-conformity under ISM element 9, with root-cause analysis - this is required whether or not the detention is disputed
start rectification in parallel with the dispute; the fastest route to sea is a rectified deficiency, not a won argument

steps.title: Putting the disagreement on the record while the detention stands
points: request the flag Administration's involvement at once - paragraph 3.5.2 requires the PSCO to notify the flag State in writing with the inspection report
the flag State may consult the port State, and paragraph 2.3.8 records that involving flag, RO and owner avoids later arguments about the circumstances of the detention
call the recognized organization that issued the certificate in question - the deficiency may impugn its survey and it has both standing and expertise
ask for re-inspection by, or in the presence of, a senior officer of the authority where the technical point is genuinely arguable
where a deficiency cannot be rectified at the port, paragraph 3.7.3 allows the authority to permit passage to the nearest appropriate repair yard chosen by the master and agreed by the authority
that route runs on conditions agreed between port State and flag State, which may include flag State confirmation that remedial action has been taken
keep a contemporaneous factual log of every exchange - times, names, what was said, what was produced
avoid asserting undue delay early; paragraph 2.3.8 shows the port State is already alive to it, and the claim is stronger made afterwards on a complete record

steps.title: Reviewing the detention - what IMO provides, and what the Panel is
points: start with what A.1185(33) actually gives - paragraph 2.3.11: the company or its representative has a right of appeal, the appeal does not suspend the detention, and the PSCO must properly inform the master of the right
chapter 5 of the Procedures is Review Procedures but it is NOT an appeal body - it is a reporting and evaluation mechanism
5.1.1 - the Organization summarises deficiency reports and disseminates them, indicating flag State action or an outstanding flag State comment
5.1.2 and 5.1.3 - the appropriate committee periodically evaluates the summary and recommendations feed back into the instruments
so IMO reviews the SYSTEM; the individual detention is reviewed regionally
the DETENTION REVIEW PANEL is a mechanism of the regional port State control memoranda of understanding, not of IMO - India participates in the Indian Ocean MOU
the shape of the process: a written application by the company or the flag State that the detention was improperly imposed, within the time the MOU allows
the application is supported by the inspection report, the certificates, the technical evidence and the flag State's position
the Panel reviews the record and the parties' submissions and reports its findings to the detaining authority and the MOU committee
the outcome is the correction of the detention record - the detention is not undone in time, which is why the record matters commercially

steps.title: The roles of the company, the flag State and class
points: the COMPANY holds the right of appeal under 2.3.11 and is the applicant - it funds, instructs and assembles the case
the company also owns the ISM consequence: the non-conformity, the root cause and the corrective action, which the flag State will look for
the FLAG STATE is the ship's principal advocate and the only party in a State-to-State relationship with the detaining authority
it receives the written detention report under 3.5.2, may seek and contest particulars, and agrees the conditions for any repair-yard passage under 3.7.3
the CLASSIFICATION SOCIETY appears in two capacities and they must be kept apart
as CLASS it certifies against its own rules; as RECOGNIZED ORGANIZATION it acted for the flag State in issuing the statutory certificate now challenged
3.3.2 and 3.5.2 require the RO to be notified where appropriate, and its survey record is often the decisive technical evidence
its own performance is engaged - a detention against a certificate it issued is a matter for the flag State's oversight of it
the three roles are complementary, not alternative: the company applies, the flag State speaks, class proves

questions.memory_cue: Two thresholds and one hard rule. The thresholds are CLEAR GROUNDS to look deeper (1) and DETAINABLE to hold the ship (2). The hard rule is APPEAL WITHOUT STAY — which is why the on-board answer is cooperate, record, rectify (3, 4) and the shore answer is company applies, flag speaks, class proves (5, 6).

quick_revision.recall_15s: A.1185(33), Procedures for Port State Control, 2023, adopted 6 December 2023. Clear grounds (1.7.2) = evidence that ship, equipment or crew do not correspond substantially with the conventions, or that master or crew are not familiar with essential shipboard procedures. Without them, inspection is limited to certificates, documents and an overall impression (2.4.1); with them, a more detailed inspection follows (2.5.1). Nine grounds at 2.4.2, expressly not exhaustive — five about things, four about people. On a disputed detention: you get an appeal but no stay (2.3.11), and the right is the company's. So cooperate, ask for the convention reference and the detainable ground for each item, sign for receipt not agreement, gather evidence, produce any Exemption Certificate (1.2.6), notify company and DPA, raise an ISM element 9 non-conformity, and rectify in parallel. Flag State and RO are notified in writing by the PSCO on detention (3.5.2). If it cannot be fixed here, 3.7.3 allows passage to the nearest appropriate repair yard on agreed conditions. The Detention Review Panel is a regional MOU body, not IMO — chapter 5 of the Procedures reviews the system, not the ship. Company applies, flag State speaks, class proves; the remedy is correction of the record.
critical_numbers: A.1185(33) adopted 6 December 2023 by the 33rd IMO Assembly
Paragraph 2.4.2 enumerates NINE clear grounds, expressly not exhaustive
Paragraph 1.7.2 - the definition of clear grounds
Paragraph 2.3.11 - right of appeal, no suspension of the detention
Paragraph 3.5.2 - flag Administration notified immediately and in writing
Paragraph 3.7.3 - nearest appropriate repair yard, chosen by the master, agreed by the authority
Chapter 5 has one section, 5.1, Report of comments
quick_revision.critical_regulation: Resolution A.1185(33) paragraph 2.4.1 read with 1.7.2 and 2.5.1 — absent clear grounds an inspection is limited to verifying valid certificates and documentation and forming an impression of overall condition; clear grounds, being evidence of substantial non-correspondence or of unfamiliarity with essential shipboard procedures, unlock the more detailed inspection. Paragraph 2.3.11 then governs any dispute: the company has a right of appeal and the appeal does not suspend the detention.
quick_revision.major_trap: Believing that disputing a detention holds it in abeyance. Paragraph 2.3.11 states expressly that the appeal should not cause the detention to be suspended, so the ship stays where it is while the argument runs — which is why the correct conduct is to rectify and dispute in parallel rather than to refuse cooperation. The paired trap is looking for the Detention Review Panel inside A.1185(33): chapter 5 is headed 'Review Procedures' but reviews the SYSTEM through summarised deficiency reports and periodic committee evaluation, while the Panel that reviews an individual detention is a regional memorandum of understanding mechanism.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Define 'clear grounds' as the Procedures for Port State Control define it.
retrieval_cards.answer: A.1185(33) paragraph 1.7.2: evidence that the ship, its equipment or its crew do not correspond substantially with the requirements of the relevant conventions, or that the master or crew members are not familiar with essential shipboard procedures relating to the safety of ships or the prevention of pollution.
retrieval_cards.why: It is a printed four-mark limb and the definition is worth stating close to the text.

retrieval_cards.prompt: What is a PSCO limited to when there are NO clear grounds?
retrieval_cards.answer: Paragraph 2.4.1: verifying that valid certificates and other relevant documentation are on board, and forming an impression of the overall condition of the ship, its equipment and its crew. Clear grounds are not needed to board - they are needed to go beyond that.
retrieval_cards.why: This is what gives the term its force, and it is the half of limb (a) most candidates omit.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Give six of the nine clear grounds in paragraph 2.4.2.
retrieval_cards.answer: Absence of principal equipment or arrangements; evidence a certificate is invalid; required documents absent, incomplete, not maintained or falsely maintained; serious hull or structural deterioration risking structural, watertight or weathertight integrity; serious deficiencies in safety, pollution prevention or navigational equipment; master or crew not familiar with essential shipboard operations. Also: key crew unable to communicate; uncancelled false distress alerts; a report or complaint that the ship appears substandard. The list is expressly not exhaustive.
retrieval_cards.why: The marks in limb (a) are in the enumeration, and five of the nine are about hardware while four are about people.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Does lodging an appeal against a detention suspend it, and whose right is it?
retrieval_cards.answer: No. Paragraph 2.3.11: the company or its representative has a right of appeal, the appeal should not cause the detention to be suspended, and the PSCO should properly inform the master of the right. The right belongs to the company, not to the master or the ship.
retrieval_cards.why: It is the single rule that determines the whole of the correct conduct - rectify and dispute in parallel.

retrieval_cards.prompt: What is the difference between a deficiency and a detainable deficiency, and why does it matter on board?
retrieval_cards.answer: A ship may sail with recorded deficiencies; it may not sail with a detainable one. Under 3.7.2 detention attaches to deficiencies clearly hazardous to safety or the environment, and 3.5.1 concedes that a ship cannot be defined as substandard solely by a list of defects. So the question to ask at the closing meeting is not 'is this a deficiency?' but 'on what basis is this deficiency detainable?', item by item, with the convention reference.
retrieval_cards.why: It is where a disputed detention is actually won, and it turns a complaint into a case.

retrieval_cards.prompt: List the immediate on-board actions when you disagree with a detention.
retrieval_cards.answer: Cooperate; attend the closing meeting and ask for the convention reference and the detainable ground for each item; obtain and check Forms A and B; sign for receipt not agreement and record the disagreement in writing; gather certificates, survey reports, PMS records, test logs and photographs at once; produce any Exemption Certificate or approved alternative design documentation under 1.2.6; notify the company and DPA; raise an ISM element 9 non-conformity; and begin rectification in parallel.
retrieval_cards.why: Cooperate, record, notify, rectify - four verbs that carry the six marks of limb (b).

retrieval_cards.prompt: Whom must the PSCO notify on detaining a ship, how, and when?
retrieval_cards.answer: Paragraph 3.5.2: the flag Administration immediately and in writing, including the report of inspection; and the recognized organization that issued the relevant certificates on behalf of the flag State, where appropriate. Both are also notified in writing of the release of detention.
retrieval_cards.why: It puts the flag State and the RO into the process from the first moment, which is what makes the later challenge possible.

retrieval_cards.prompt: The deficiency cannot be repaired in the port of detention. What does A.1185(33) allow?
retrieval_cards.answer: Paragraph 3.7.3: the port State authority may allow the ship to proceed to the nearest appropriate repair yard available, chosen by the master and agreed by that authority, provided the conditions agreed between the port State and the flag State are complied with - which may include flag State confirmation that remedial action has been taken. The next port and other authorities are notified.
retrieval_cards.why: It is the practical escape from an unrepairable detention and is routinely omitted.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Is the Detention Review Panel established by A.1185(33)?
retrieval_cards.answer: No. A.1185(33) chapter 5 is headed 'Review Procedures' but is a systemic mechanism - the Organization summarises deficiency reports, the appropriate committee periodically evaluates them, and recommendations feed back into the instruments. The Detention Review Panel is a mechanism of the regional port State control memoranda of understanding; India participates in the Indian Ocean MOU.
retrieval_cards.why: The stem invites the assumption that it is an IMO body, and drawing the IMO/MOU boundary is what distinguishes a good limb (c).

retrieval_cards.prompt: In a detention review, what does each of the company, the flag State and the classification society do?
retrieval_cards.answer: The company holds the right of appeal, instructs and funds the challenge, assembles the technical case and owns the ISM corrective action. The flag State is the ship's principal advocate and the only party in a State-to-State relationship with the detaining authority; it receives the detention report, contests particulars and agrees any repair-yard conditions. The classification society acts in two capacities - as class against its own rules, and as recognized organization which issued the statutory certificate now challenged and supplies the decisive survey evidence.
retrieval_cards.why: Company applies, flag speaks, class proves - and the two hats of the society are a standing distinction.

retrieval_cards.prompt: What does a successful detention review actually achieve?
retrieval_cards.answer: Correction of the record - deletion or amendment of the detention entry in the regional database. It does not restore the lost time and does not of itself award compensation. That matters because the detention entry drives the ship's and company's targeting factor and is read by charterers and vetting inspectors for years afterwards.
retrieval_cards.why: It explains why the process is pursued at all, and stops the answer promising a remedy the system does not give.

questions.text_verbatim: Explain the concept of underwater radiated noise (URN) generated by ships. Identify its primary sources and discuss the effects of such noise on marine life. (8) b) Describe the international guidelines and best practices aimed at reducing underwater noise (e.g., IMO MEPC.1/Circ.833). What operational, design and maintenance measures can be implemented to minimize underwater noise? Also, explain the role of the Chief Engineer in ensuring compliance. (8)

subparts.text: Explain underwater radiated noise (URN) generated by ships, identify its primary sources, and discuss its effects on marine life.
The international guidelines and best practices for reducing underwater noise, the operational, design and maintenance measures available, and the role of the Chief Engineer in ensuring compliance.

decomposition: What underwater radiated noise is, and how it is described and measured
The primary sources on a merchant ship, ranked by contribution and by speed dependence
The effects on marine life, separated into the four mechanisms rather than listed loosely
The international framework - the circular the stem names, its revision, and the crucial fact that the whole regime is recommendatory
Design measures - hull form, propeller, and machinery mounting
Operational and maintenance measures, including the ones a Chief Engineer actually controls
The Chief Engineer's role in ensuring compliance, expressed through the management system rather than as a list of good intentions

PRIMARY: MARPOL Annex VI regulation 26 - every ship of the relevant class shall keep on board a Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan. The corpus record MARPOLVI_REG26 confirms the duty is unconditional in time from the Annex's entry into force and sets out the plan's content structure. The SEEMP is the document in which voluntary efficiency and noise measures are recorded, and it is the mechanism by which the Chief Engineer's role becomes auditable.

PRIMARY: MARPOL Annex VI regulation 22 - the Energy Efficiency Design Index applies to new ships, establishing that hull and propulsive efficiency are already a design-stage regulatory subject; the overlap between efficiency and quieting is real and is the strongest practical argument for URN measures.

AUTHORITATIVE SECONDARY: MEPC.1/Circ.833, the 2014 Guidelines for the reduction of underwater noise from commercial shipping to address adverse impacts on marine life - the instrument the printed stem names. Recommendatory, addressed to designers, shipbuilders and operators, and directed principally at propeller cavitation, hull form and onboard machinery.

AUTHORITATIVE SECONDARY: MEPC.1/Circ.906, the Revised guidelines approved at MEPC 80 in 2023, which superseded MEPC.1/Circ.833. The revision restructures the guidance around a URN Management Plan, addresses measurement and target-setting, and is accompanied by an Action Plan and a three-year Experience Building Phase intended to gather data before any further step is considered. NOT HELD BY THE CORPUS - flagged for currency check.
AUTHORITATIVE SECONDARY: ISO 17208-1 and ISO 17208-2, the measurement standards for underwater sound from ships in deep water, referenced by the guidelines as the basis for comparable measurement.

AUTHORITATIVE SECONDARY: UNCLOS article 1(1)(4) defines pollution of the marine environment by reference to the INTRODUCTION OF ENERGY, which is why noise is capable of being pollution in international law at all, and article 194 obliges States to prevent, reduce and control it from vessels.

ENGINEERING JUDGEMENT (mechanism only, no quantified figures): the source hierarchy - propeller cavitation dominant above inception speed, machinery-borne noise dominant below it, hydrodynamic flow noise third; the strong non-linear dependence of cavitation noise on speed; the broadband versus tonal signature distinction; and the overlap between quieting measures and fuel efficiency measures.
INDUSTRY GUIDANCE: class notations for underwater radiated noise exist and are voluntary; they are named as a category rather than by society, because no class rulebook is held by the corpus.

No decibel value, source-level figure, frequency band or reduction target is given anywhere in this answer. Underwater sound levels are expressed in dB re 1 microPascal at 1 m and are entirely ship-, speed- and condition-specific. Quoting a number from memory would be false precision of exactly the kind the production protocol forbids.

No quantified noise reduction is attributed to any mitigation measure. Gains from propeller redesign, hull-form change, resilient mounting or air lubrication are installation-specific and vendor-sourced. Mechanism and direction only.

The dates and current status of the IMO Action Plan and the Experience Building Phase are stated in outline only. The IMO documents recording them are not held, so the answer states the shape of the programme and not its milestones.

Species-specific hearing ranges and behavioural thresholds are not quoted. The biological literature is outside the corpus entirely and thresholds are contested; the answer describes the four mechanisms of harm rather than assigning numbers to them.
Class notation designations for underwater radiated noise are not named. No classification society rulebook is held by the corpus.

blocks.h: (a) The concept of URN, its primary sources and its effects on marine life — 8 marks (the source copy prints no limb letter here)
1. What underwater radiated noise is, and how it is described

blocks.p: Underwater radiated noise (URN) is the sound a ship puts into the sea as an unintended by-product of propulsion, machinery operation and motion through the water. It is not deliberately produced and, critically, nothing is discharged — which is why it falls entirely outside the MARPOL discharge model and had to be approached through guidelines rather than through an Annex.

It is nonetheless capable of being pollution in international law, because UNCLOS article 1(1)(4) defines pollution of the marine environment as the introduction of substances or energy into the marine environment resulting in deleterious effects. Sound is energy, and article 194 obliges States to prevent, reduce and control pollution from vessels.
URN is described as a source level — in decibels referred to one micropascal at one metre — expressed as a spectrum across frequency. Three properties matter:

ul: shipping noise is overwhelmingly low frequency, and low frequency propagates enormous distances, particularly in the deep sound channel — so a ship is heard far beyond the horizon;
the signature has two components: broadband noise from cavitation and turbulence, and discrete tonal peaks at shaft rate, blade rate and engine firing orders; and
measurement is standardised — ISO 17208-1 and 17208-2 — so that ships can be compared at all.

blocks.p: The concern is not one loud ship. It is the cumulative raising of the ambient noise floor across whole ocean basins by continuous merchant traffic, sustained over decades.

blocks.h: 2. The primary sources on a merchant ship

blocks.p: There are three source groups, and which one dominates depends on the operating condition:

rows: Vapour cavities form in low-pressure regions on the blade and collapse violently, radiating broadband noise. Tip vortex cavitation is usually first to appear and often the loudest single mechanism
Above cavitation inception speed — i.e. at normal service speed, where it swamps everything else
Main engine, gearbox, generators, pumps and compressors; structure-borne vibration transmitted through mounts, seatings and shell plating and re-radiated into the water. Carries the tonal content
Below cavitation inception, at low speed, at anchor and in dynamic positioning
Turbulent boundary layer over hull and appendages, flow over sea chests, openings and the bow wave
Third in magnitude for most merchant ships — but it creates the wake the propeller works in, so it feeds source one

blocks.p: Cavitation is worsened by a non-uniform wake, by blade damage, roughness and fouling, and by operating off the design point — heavy loading, unusual trim, poor immersion. And the property that governs the whole of limb (b) is its strong non-linearity: cavitation noise rises very steeply with speed, so a modest reduction in speed produces a large reduction in radiated noise.

blocks.h: 3. The effects on marine life

blocks.p: The harm is not a single phenomenon, and separating the mechanisms is what earns the marks here:

ol: Masking. Shipping noise occupies the same low frequencies that baleen whales and many fish use for communication, navigation and prey detection. It drowns out biologically important sound, shrinking the range over which animals can hear one another — a measurable loss of acoustic habitat. This is the principal chronic effect.

Behavioural disturbance. Avoidance of shipping lanes and displacement from preferred habitat; interrupted feeding; disrupted breeding, nursing and mother–calf contact; altered diving and vocalisation.
Physiological stress. Chronic exposure is associated with elevated stress responses, with downstream consequences for immune function, health and reproductive success.
Auditory injury. Temporary or permanent threshold shift close to a powerful source. This is a proximity effect and is not the principal shipping concern, which is chronic and diffuse.

blocks.p: The range of affected animals is broad: marine mammals, which are the usual focus; fish, including commercially important species whose spawning aggregations are noise-sensitive; and invertebrates, many of which sense particle motion rather than pressure. The defining characteristic of the problem is that it is cumulative and chronic rather than acute.

blocks.h: (b) International guidelines, mitigation measures and the Chief Engineer’s role — 8 marks
4. The international framework - and the fact that it is entirely recommendatory

blocks.p: State the status first, because it governs everything else: there is no mandatory IMO requirement on underwater radiated noise at this sitting. MARPOL Annex VI contains no provision on it. This is a guidelines regime, addressed to designers, shipbuilders and operators, not a compliance regime with a limit to be met and a certificate to be held.

The printed question names MEPC.1/Circ.833, the 2014 Guidelines for the reduction of underwater noise from commercial shipping to address adverse impacts on marine life. That circular established the framework: it identified propeller cavitation as the dominant source, and directed designers and operators to hull form and wake field, propeller design, and onboard machinery, together with operational and maintenance considerations.

The currency point must be made. Circ.833 was superseded by the Revised guidelines, MEPC.1/Circ.906, approved at MEPC 80 in 2023 — roughly two years before this examination, so the revised circular is the operative edition at this sitting. The revision restructures the guidance around a URN Management Plan, and gives greater attention to measurement, establishing a baseline and setting reduction targets. It is accompanied by an Action Plan and a three-year Experience Building Phase intended to gather data and practical experience before any further step is considered. That phase is running at this sitting and has not reported, so nothing can be said about what may follow it.

Around the IMO layer sit UNCLOS article 194; the ISO 17208 measurement standards; voluntary class notations for underwater radiated noise; and port and coastal incentive schemes that reward quiet ships in sensitive waters.

blocks.h: 5. Design measures

blocks.p: These are newbuilding and major-conversion measures. A serving Chief Engineer influences them chiefly through feedback and specification, but they must be known.

Propeller — the most productive single target, because it is the dominant source. Increased blade area ratio and skew; optimised pitch distribution and blade section; control of tip loading to delay cavitation inception. The design objective is to raise cavitation inception speed above the ship’s normal service speed, so that the loudest mechanism does not occur in normal operation at all.

Hull form — give the propeller clean water. Aftbody lines optimised for wake-field uniformity; wake-equalising ducts, pre-swirl stators and fin arrangements; and adequate propeller–hull clearance. A propeller in a badly disturbed wake cavitates unsteadily and is loud however well it is designed.

Machinery — break the structure-borne path. Resilient mounting of main and auxiliary machinery, including double-resilient arrangements for the noisiest units; flexible couplings and flexible pipe connections; acoustic isolation of seatings; damping treatments on radiating structure; and low-noise selection of pumps, fans and compressors. Diesel-electric or hybrid propulsion decouples engine speed from shaft speed and is often markedly quieter at low speed. Air lubrication and hull coatings contribute, and voluntary class notations exist to formalise the whole target at the design stage.

blocks.h: 6. Operational and maintenance measures, and the Chief Engineer's role

blocks.p: Operational measures. Speed reduction is the most powerful single lever available, precisely because cavitation noise rises so steeply with speed. Alongside it: routeing to avoid known sensitive habitats and participation in voluntary slowdown schemes where they operate; avoiding operation far off the design point and avoiding heavy propeller loading and excessive rudder movement; trim and draught optimisation to keep the propeller properly immersed in clean inflow; and machinery load management so that nothing unnecessary is running.
Maintenance measures — and this is where the Chief Engineer’s real influence lies. Everything here is within the department’s control:

ul: Hull cleaning and propeller polishing on measured condition, not to the calendar. Fouling roughens the blade surface and disturbs the inflow, advancing cavitation inception — a fouled ship is both slower and louder.
Propeller blade edge repair. Even minor edge damage or erosion is acoustically significant out of all proportion to its hydrodynamic cost.
Shaft alignment and bearing condition, and correction of imbalance and misalignment, which generate the tonal components of the signature.

Resilient mount condition. Mounts that are degraded, oil-soaked, bottomed-out or bridged by a rigid pipe or cable run short-circuit the acoustic isolation designed into the ship — an entirely invisible failure with a large acoustic cost.
Flexible couplings and pipe connections maintained so that structure-borne paths are not inadvertently rigidly bridged during repairs.
Vibration monitoring used as an acoustic proxy — a rise in structure-borne vibration is generally a rise in radiated noise, and the ship already has the instrumentation.

blocks.p: The Chief Engineer’s role in ensuring compliance must be expressed through the management system, not as a list of good intentions — and it is shaped by the fact that the regime is voluntary. There is no certificate to hold and no survey to pass, so the discipline has to be self-imposed and auditable. Concretely, the Chief Engineer should:

ol: Document the measures where they can be audited — in the SEEMP, whose keeping on board is a duty under MARPOL Annex VI regulation 26, and in the URN Management Plan where the company keeps one under the revised guidelines;

Bring it into the safety management system under the ISM Code as an environmental protection objective, with procedures for hull and propeller condition management, mount inspection and vibration monitoring, and with training and reporting to match;
Advise the master and the company where speed and routeing are the effective controls, since those are commercial decisions that the engine room can inform but not take; and

Make the efficiency argument. Almost every measure that quietens a ship — a clean hull, a polished propeller, optimised trim, reduced speed, well-matched machinery load — also reduces fuel consumption, cuts CO2 and improves the ship’s CII rating. That overlap is what turns a voluntary environmental measure into something a company will actually fund, and stating it is the strongest close available to this answer.

blocks.h: Why this structure scores

blocks.p: The printed question is unlimbed at the top — it runs straight from “Q3.” into the first task and prints “(8)” at its end, with only the second limb labelled “b)”. That is a source anomaly, it is preserved, and the answer simply gives the first limb a descriptive heading without inventing an “(a)” the paper does not print.

Limb (a) sets three tasks — concept, sources, effects — and each has a section. The sources go in a table because the examinable point is not the list but the condition dependence: cavitation above inception, machinery below it. A table shows that in one glance; prose buries it.

Limb (b) also sets three tasks, and the measures task is deliberately split into design and operational/maintenance. That split is not cosmetic: it separates what a Chief Engineer can only influence from what a Chief Engineer actually controls, which is exactly what the third task — the role — is asking about.

blocks.h: The one physical fact that organises the whole question

blocks.p: Propeller cavitation dominates above inception speed, and cavitation noise rises very steeply with speed.

Almost every mark in this question can be derived from that sentence. It explains why the propeller is the top source and the design priority. It explains why slowing down is the single most powerful mitigation. It explains why hull fouling and blade damage matter acoustically — they advance inception. It explains why the sources reorder at low speed and at anchor, where machinery-borne noise takes over. And it explains the efficiency overlap, since the same conditions that cause cavitation also waste power.

blocks.h: Answer the circular the paper names - then say which one is current

blocks.p: The stem cites MEPC.1/Circ.833, which is the 2014 guidelines and was superseded by the revised circular MEPC.1/Circ.906, approved at MEPC 80 in 2023. Both dates are before this sitting.

The right technique — in the examination and in this answer — is not to correct the examiner and not to answer only on the superseded text. Name the circular the paper names, describe what it established, and then state plainly that the revised guidelines are the operative edition at the time of writing. The stem itself says “e.g.”, so it is not insisting on that circular exclusively. A candidate who does this cannot be marked wrong on either edition and picks up a currency mark that most will miss.

blocks.h: There is no regulation here, and saying so is worth marks

blocks.p: This is the most commonly mishandled feature of the question. Candidates write about URN as though it were regulated — “compliance with the noise limits”, “the noise certificate” — and there is no limit and no certificate. At April 2025 the regime is wholly recommendatory. MARPOL Annex VI, which is the natural place to look, contains nothing on it.

That changes what “the role of the Chief Engineer in ensuring compliance” can even mean. There is no statutory compliance to ensure. What there is, is company policy, management-system governance and documentation — which is why the answer routes the role through the SEEMP, the URN Management Plan and the ISM environmental objective, all of which are auditable, rather than through a survey that does not exist.

blocks.h: The four mechanisms of harm - do not write one blur

blocks.p: “It disturbs whales” is worth very little. Four named mechanisms are worth a great deal more, and they are genuinely distinct:

ul: Masking — the chronic, population-scale effect, and the one that matters most for shipping. Loss of communication range is loss of acoustic habitat.
Behavioural disturbance — avoidance, displacement, interrupted feeding and breeding.
Physiological stress — chronic, sub-lethal, with reproductive consequences.
Auditory injury — threshold shift, but only close to a powerful source, and therefore not the main shipping issue.

blocks.p: Add breadth beyond mammals: fish, whose spawning aggregations are noise-sensitive, and invertebrates, which largely detect particle motion rather than pressure — a distinction that shows real reading.

blocks.h: Common mistakes

ul: Treating URN as a regulated emission with limits and a certificate. It is recommendatory at this sitting.
Looking for it in MARPOL. Nothing in Annex VI or any other Annex addresses underwater noise.
Naming machinery as the dominant source. It dominates only below cavitation inception — at service speed the propeller dominates.
Quoting decibel figures or source levels from memory. They are ship-, speed- and condition-specific, and a wrong number is worse than none.
Writing the effects as one undifferentiated statement instead of four mechanisms.
Giving only newbuilding design measures. The examiner asks for operational, design and maintenance measures — and the Chief Engineer's marks are in the last two.
Omitting hull and propeller condition. Fouling and blade damage are acoustic problems, not just efficiency ones.
Forgetting resilient mount condition, which is the classic invisible failure — an isolation system defeated by an oil-soaked mount or a rigid pipe bridging it.
Saying only that Circ.833 applies, when the revised guidelines govern at this sitting; or conversely, ignoring Circ.833 when the paper names it.
Missing the closing argument — that quieting and fuel efficiency very largely coincide.

blocks.h: Examiner traps

ul: “Which MARPOL Annex covers underwater noise?” None. It is a guidelines subject and there is no mandatory instrument.
“How can noise be pollution if nothing is discharged?” UNCLOS article 1(1)(4) defines pollution to include the introduction of energy into the marine environment.
“What is the loudest thing on your ship, acoustically?” The propeller, once cavitating — above cavitation inception speed. Below it, the machinery.
“Your ship is at anchor with one generator running. What is the source?” Machinery-borne, structure-borne into the hull and re-radiated. No cavitation, so the ranking inverts.
“You reduce speed by 10%. What happens to the noise?” It falls disproportionately, because cavitation noise depends very strongly on speed. Give the mechanism, not a number.
“Does a foul hull make a ship noisier?” Yes — roughness and disturbed wake advance cavitation inception and make cavitation more unsteady.
“What is tip vortex cavitation?” Cavitation in the vortex shed from the blade tip; usually the first to appear as loading increases, and often the loudest single mechanism.
“Where would you record your URN measures?” In the SEEMP, and in the URN Management Plan under the revised guidelines; and as an environmental objective in the SMS.
“Why would an owner spend money on this when it is voluntary?” Because nearly every measure also saves fuel and improves CII, and because port incentive schemes and charterer expectations reward it.

blocks.h: Likely oral follow-up

ul: What does URN stand for and how is it expressed? Underwater radiated noise; source level in dB re 1 micropascal at 1 m, as a spectrum.
Name the three source groups in order of importance at service speed. Propeller cavitation, machinery-borne noise, hydrodynamic flow noise.
Which IMO circular does the syllabus name, and which edition is current? MEPC.1/Circ.833 (2014); the revised guidelines MEPC.1/Circ.906, approved at MEPC 80 in 2023.
Is compliance mandatory? No - the regime is recommendatory.
Name four ways noise harms marine life. Masking, behavioural disturbance, physiological stress, auditory injury.
Give three maintenance measures within your control. Hull cleaning and propeller polishing on condition; propeller blade edge repair; resilient mount and alignment condition.
What single operational measure helps most? Speed reduction.
Where do the measures get documented? SEEMP, URN Management Plan, and the SMS as an environmental objective.

blocks.h: Memory framework

blocks.p: For the sources, three words in descending order at service speed: PROPELLER, MACHINERY, FLOW — and one caveat: the order inverts at low speed.
For the effects, four words: MASK, MOVE, STRESS, INJURE. Masking is the chronic one that matters; injury is the acute one that mostly does not.
For the measures, work down the ship: PROPELLER → HULL → MACHINERY for design; SPEED → ROUTE → CONDITION for operations and maintenance.
And carry one closing sentence, because it is the highest-value thing in the answer: a quiet ship is usually an efficient ship.

blocks.h: Regulation and source map

ul: MEPC.1/Circ.833 — 2014 Guidelines for the reduction of underwater noise from commercial shipping to address adverse impacts on marine life. The circular the printed stem names.

MEPC.1/Circ.906 — Revised guidelines on the reduction of underwater radiated noise from shipping, approved at MEPC 80 (2023); supersedes Circ.833 and is the operative edition at this sitting. Accompanied by an Action Plan and a three-year Experience Building Phase, which is running and has not reported.

MARPOL Annex VI — contains no provision on underwater radiated noise. Regulation 26 requires the SEEMP, which is where voluntary measures are documented; regulation 22 is the EEDI, establishing propulsive efficiency as a design-stage subject.
UNCLOS article 1(1)(4) — pollution includes the introduction of energy. Article 194 — the duty to prevent, reduce and control pollution from vessels.
ISO 17208-1 and 17208-2 — measurement of underwater sound from ships.
ISM Code — element 1.2.2 (safety and environmental protection objectives) and element 7 (shipboard operations) are the hooks for making a voluntary measure auditable.
Voluntary class notations and port incentive schemes — named as categories; no society or scheme is identified, because none is held.

blocks.h: Uncertainty and the limits of the evidence

blocks.p: This question rests on the thinnest corpus evidence of any on the paper, and that is stated rather than concealed. Neither MEPC.1/Circ.833 nor MEPC.1/Circ.906 is held by the True Source corpus in any form — a full-text search for both circular numbers and for “underwater radiated noise” returns nothing. Their identity, dates, supersession and structure are therefore carried at authoritative-secondary level and are flagged for currency check before publication.

What IS primary is the negative, and it is the most important single statement in the answer. MARPOL Annex VI is held complete, verified against the official IMO resolutions and frozen, with its amendment chain closed through MEPC.392(82) — and it contains no provision on underwater radiated noise. The absence of a mandatory requirement is therefore established from a complete instrument rather than inferred from silence in a partial one.
No paragraph of either circular is cited by number, because that precision cannot be sourced. No recommendation is attributed to a specific paragraph.

No decibel value, source level, frequency band or reduction target appears anywhere in this answer, and no quantified noise reduction is attributed to any mitigation measure. Underwater sound levels are wholly ship-, speed- and condition-specific, and mitigation gains are installation-specific and vendor-sourced. The answer gives mechanism and direction only, which is a deliberate application of the production protocol’s rule against false precision.

No species-specific hearing range or behavioural threshold is quoted. The biological literature is outside the corpus and the thresholds are contested; the answer describes the four mechanisms rather than assigning numbers to them.

Currency. The position stated is that at April 2025: the revised guidelines are the operative edition, the Experience Building Phase is running and has not reported, and there is no mandatory measure. Nothing is asserted about what may follow. MEPC 83 sat inside this sitting month and adopted its resolutions on 11 April 2025, but none of its outputs touches this subject, so this question’s correctness does not depend on the examination day. Instruments postdating April 2025 are absent.

questions.understand_first: The examinable idea is that a ship is an acoustic source whether anyone intended it or not, and that almost everything which makes it loud also makes it inefficient. Underwater radiated noise is not an emission in the MARPOL sense — nothing is discharged — but international law can still treat it as pollution, because UNCLOS defines pollution of the marine environment to include the introduction of energy. The mechanism is dominated by one thing: propeller cavitation. Below the speed at which cavitation begins, a ship is a relatively quiet machinery-noise source; above it, collapsing vapour bubbles generate broadband noise that rises steeply with speed and swamps everything else. That single fact organises the whole answer — it explains why the sources rank as they do, why slowing down is the most powerful single measure, why hull and propeller condition matter as much as design, and why the measures overlap so heavily with fuel-efficiency measures. And the regulatory point to hold on to is that none of it is mandatory at this sitting: the guidance is recommendatory, which changes the Chief Engineer's role from compliance to management-system governance.

steps.title: What underwater radiated noise is, and how it is described
points: URN is the sound a ship puts into the water as an unintended by-product of propulsion, machinery and motion through the sea
it is not a discharge - nothing leaves the ship - so it falls outside the MARPOL discharge model entirely
UNCLOS article 1(1)(4) defines pollution of the marine environment to include the introduction of ENERGY, which is what makes noise capable of being pollution in law
described as a source level, in decibels referred to one micropascal at one metre, as a spectrum across frequency
shipping noise is overwhelmingly LOW FREQUENCY, and low frequency travels far in the deep sound channel
the signature has two parts - broadband noise from cavitation and turbulence, and discrete tones from rotating machinery and blade rate
measurement is standardised by ISO 17208-1 and 17208-2 so that ships can be compared at all
the cumulative point - the concern is not one ship but the raised ambient noise floor across whole ocean basins

steps.title: The primary sources on a merchant ship
points: three source groups, and which one dominates depends on the operating condition
PROPELLER CAVITATION - the dominant source above cavitation inception speed
vapour cavities form in the low-pressure regions on the blade and collapse violently, radiating broadband noise
tip vortex cavitation is usually the first to appear and often the loudest single mechanism
it is worsened by a non-uniform wake, by blade damage, roughness and fouling, and by operating off the design point
MACHINERY-BORNE NOISE - main engine, gearbox, generators, pumps and compressors, transmitted through mounts, seatings and the hull into the water
this is structure-borne noise become waterborne; it dominates BELOW cavitation inception, and at anchor or in DP
it carries the discrete tonal content, at shaft and blade rate and at engine firing orders
HYDRODYNAMIC FLOW NOISE - turbulent boundary layer over the hull, appendages, sea chests, openings and bow wave
third in magnitude for most merchant ships but it is what the propeller inflow is made of, so it feeds source one
the key non-linearity - cavitation noise rises very steeply with speed, so a small speed reduction is a large noise reduction

steps.title: The effects on marine life
points: the harm is not one phenomenon; separate it into four mechanisms, because that is what earns the marks
MASKING - shipping noise occupies the same low frequencies that baleen whales and many fish use, so it drowns out communication, navigation and prey detection
masking reduces the effective range over which animals can hear each other - the loss of acoustic habitat
BEHAVIOURAL DISTURBANCE - avoidance of shipping lanes, interrupted feeding, disrupted breeding and nursing, displacement from preferred habitat
PHYSIOLOGICAL STRESS - chronic exposure is associated with elevated stress responses, with consequences for health and reproduction
AUDITORY INJURY - temporary or permanent threshold shift close to a powerful source; this is a proximity effect, not the main shipping concern
the affected range is broad - marine mammals, fish, and invertebrates that sense particle motion rather than pressure
the cumulative and chronic character is the real issue - a raised ambient noise floor along busy routes, sustained over decades
no threshold figures are quoted here - they are species-specific and contested

steps.title: The international framework - and the fact that it is entirely recommendatory
points: state the status FIRST because it governs everything else - there is no mandatory IMO requirement on URN at this sitting
MARPOL Annex VI, held complete and verified, contains no provision on underwater radiated noise
so this is a GUIDELINES regime, addressed to designers, builders and operators, not a compliance regime
the stem names MEPC.1/Circ.833, the 2014 Guidelines for the reduction of underwater noise from commercial shipping
Circ.833 identified propeller cavitation as the dominant source and directed attention to hull form, propeller design and machinery
it was SUPERSEDED by the Revised guidelines, MEPC.1/Circ.906, approved at MEPC 80 in 2023 - the operative edition at this sitting
the revision reorganises the guidance around a URN Management Plan, addresses measurement, baselines and target-setting
it is accompanied by an Action Plan and a three-year EXPERIENCE BUILDING PHASE, which is RUNNING at this sitting and has not reported
surrounding it: UNCLOS article 194, ISO 17208 measurement standards, voluntary class notations, and port incentive schemes
name the circular the paper names, then say which edition is current - that is the correct exam technique

steps.title: Design measures
points: these are newbuilding and major-conversion measures; a serving Chief Engineer influences them mainly through feedback and specification
PROPELLER - the single most productive design target, because it is the dominant source
increased blade area and skew, optimised pitch and section, tip-loading control to delay cavitation inception
raise inception speed above the ship's normal service speed and the loudest mechanism simply does not occur in service
HULL FORM - wake-field optimisation so that the propeller sees the most uniform inflow possible
aftbody lines, wake-equalising ducts, pre-swirl stators, fin arrangements; adequate propeller-hull clearance
MACHINERY - resilient mounting of main and auxiliary machinery, double-resilient mounts, flexible couplings and pipe connections
acoustic isolation of seatings, vibration-damping treatments, low-noise selection of pumps, fans and compressors
diesel-electric or hybrid propulsion decouples engine speed from shaft speed and can be markedly quieter at low speed
air lubrication and hull coatings contribute, and voluntary class notations exist to formalise the target

steps.title: Operational and maintenance measures, and the Chief Engineer's role
points: OPERATIONAL - speed reduction is the most powerful single lever, because cavitation noise rises so steeply with speed
routeing away from known sensitive habitats, and participation in voluntary slowdown schemes where they exist
avoiding operation far off the design point, and avoiding heavy propeller loading and excessive rudder use
trim and draught optimisation to keep the propeller properly immersed and the inflow clean
load management so that unnecessary machinery is not running
MAINTENANCE - and this is where the Chief Engineer's real influence lies
hull cleaning and propeller polishing on measured condition, not on the calendar - fouling roughens inflow and advances cavitation
propeller blade edge repair; even minor damage or erosion is acoustically significant
shaft alignment and bearing condition; correction of imbalance and misalignment that generate tonal noise
resilient mount condition - degraded, oil-soaked or bottomed-out mounts short-circuit the isolation designed into the ship
maintaining flexible couplings and pipe connections so structure-borne paths are not bridged
vibration monitoring used as an acoustic proxy, since a rise in structure-borne vibration is usually a rise in radiated noise
THE CHIEF ENGINEER'S ROLE - own it through the management system, not through good intentions
document the measures in the SEEMP, whose keeping is a MARPOL Annex VI regulation 26 duty, and in the URN Management Plan where one is kept
bring it into the SMS under ISM as an environmental objective, with procedures, training and reporting
advise the master and the company where speed or routeing is the effective control, since those are commercial decisions
make the efficiency argument - almost every quieting measure also reduces fuel consumption and improves CII

questions.memory_cue: One physical fact organises everything: cavitation dominates, and it rises steeply with speed (2). So the sources rank as they do (2), the effects are cumulative (3), the regime is advisory (4), and the fix is design the propeller (5) or slow down and keep it clean (6).

Three sources: propeller cavitation dominant above inception speed (tip vortex first and loudest), machinery-borne below it and at anchor, hydrodynamic flow third. Cavitation noise rises very steeply with speed. Four harms: masking (the chronic one), behavioural disturbance, physiological stress, auditory injury. Framework: the stem names MEPC.1/Circ.833 (2014); it was superseded by the revised guidelines MEPC.1/Circ.906, MEPC 80, 2023, with an Action Plan and a three-year Experience Building Phase still running. The whole regime is recommendatory — no limit, no certificate. Design: propeller blade area, skew, tip loading to raise inception speed; wake-field and hull form; resilient mounting. Operations and maintenance: slow down, route away from sensitive habitat, clean hull and polished propeller on condition, blade edge repair, alignment, mount condition, vibration monitoring. quick_revision.critical_regulation: There is no mandatory instrument. The subject is governed by recommendatory IMO guidelines — MEPC.1/Circ.833 of 2014, superseded by the Revised guidelines MEPC.1/Circ.906 approved at MEPC 80 in 2023 — sitting beneath UNCLOS article 194 and the article 1(1)(4) definition of pollution as including the introduction of energy. MARPOL Annex VI contains nothing on underwater radiated noise, and the SEEMP required by its regulation 26 is simply the auditable document in which voluntary measures are recorded.
quick_revision.major_trap: Writing about underwater radiated noise as though it were a regulated emission — referring to noise limits, compliance and a certificate. At this sitting the regime is entirely recommendatory: there is no limit, no survey and no certificate, and MARPOL Annex VI contains no provision on it at all. The paired technical trap is naming machinery as the dominant source: machinery-borne noise dominates only below cavitation inception speed, and at normal service speed propeller cavitation swamps everything else.

retrieval_cards.prompt: What is underwater radiated noise, and how can it be pollution when nothing is discharged?
retrieval_cards.answer: Sound a ship puts into the sea as an unintended by-product of propulsion, machinery and motion through the water. It is pollution because UNCLOS article 1(1)(4) defines pollution of the marine environment to include the introduction of substances OR ENERGY resulting in deleterious effects; sound is energy. Article 194 obliges States to control it from vessels.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Name the three primary sources of ship URN and say when each dominates.
retrieval_cards.answer: Propeller cavitation - dominant above cavitation inception speed, i.e. at normal service speed, with tip vortex cavitation usually first and loudest. Machinery-borne noise - main engine, gearbox, generators, pumps, transmitted as structure-borne vibration and re-radiated; dominant below inception, at anchor and in DP, and it carries the tonal content. Hydrodynamic flow noise - boundary layer, appendages, openings; third, but it makes the wake the propeller works in.
retrieval_cards.why: The condition dependence is the examinable point; a flat list of three misses it.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Is there a mandatory IMO requirement on underwater radiated noise at April 2025?
retrieval_cards.answer: No. The regime is wholly recommendatory - guidelines addressed to designers, builders and operators, with no limit, no survey and no certificate. MARPOL Annex VI contains no provision on underwater noise at all.
retrieval_cards.why: Candidates routinely write about compliance with noise limits that do not exist, and this changes what the Chief Engineer's role can even mean.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Which circular does the syllabus name, and which edition actually governs at this sitting?
retrieval_cards.answer: The stem names MEPC.1/Circ.833, the 2014 Guidelines for the reduction of underwater noise from commercial shipping. It was superseded by the Revised guidelines MEPC.1/Circ.906, approved at MEPC 80 in 2023, which is the operative edition at this sitting and which reorganises the guidance around a URN Management Plan, measurement and target-setting.
retrieval_cards.why: Naming the circular the paper names and then stating the current edition cannot be marked wrong either way, and picks up a currency mark most candidates miss.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Give the four distinct mechanisms by which URN harms marine life.
retrieval_cards.answer: Masking - shipping noise occupies the same low frequencies animals use, drowning out communication, navigation and prey detection, and shrinking acoustic habitat. Behavioural disturbance - avoidance, displacement, interrupted feeding and breeding. Physiological stress - chronic, with reproductive consequences. Auditory injury - temporary or permanent threshold shift, but only close to a powerful source.
retrieval_cards.why: Four named mechanisms score; 'it disturbs whales' does not. Masking is the chronic effect that matters for shipping.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Why is speed reduction the single most powerful operational mitigation?
retrieval_cards.answer: Because cavitation is the dominant source at service speed and cavitation noise rises very steeply and non-linearly with speed. Reducing speed can take the ship below, or nearer to, cavitation inception, so the loudest mechanism weakens disproportionately. Give the mechanism rather than a figure - the relationship is ship-specific.
retrieval_cards.why: It is the one measure that needs no capital expenditure, and the reasoning shows the physics has been understood.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Give five maintenance measures within a Chief Engineer's direct control that reduce URN.
retrieval_cards.answer: Hull cleaning and propeller polishing planned on measured condition rather than to a calendar; propeller blade edge repair, since minor erosion is acoustically significant; shaft alignment and bearing condition, and correction of imbalance that generates tonal noise; resilient mount condition, since degraded, oil-soaked or bridged mounts defeat the designed isolation; and vibration monitoring used as an acoustic proxy.
retrieval_cards.why: This is where the Chief Engineer's marks are - design measures belong to the newbuilding, maintenance belongs to the department.

retrieval_cards.prompt: What is the design objective when a propeller is optimised for low noise?
retrieval_cards.answer: To raise the cavitation inception speed above the ship's normal service speed, so the dominant noise mechanism does not occur in ordinary operation. Achieved through increased blade area ratio and skew, optimised pitch distribution and blade section, and control of tip loading - supported by hull-form work that gives the propeller a uniform wake to work in.
retrieval_cards.why: It converts a vague 'better propeller design' into a stated engineering target.

retrieval_cards.prompt: How does a Chief Engineer 'ensure compliance' with a voluntary regime?
retrieval_cards.answer: Through the management system, because there is no survey. Document the measures in the SEEMP - which MARPOL Annex VI regulation 26 requires to be kept on board - and in the URN Management Plan where the company keeps one; embed them in the SMS under ISM as an environmental protection objective with procedures, training and reporting; advise the master and company where speed and routeing are the effective controls; and justify it on fuel, since almost every quieting measure also improves CII.
retrieval_cards.why: It answers the printed question honestly given that no statutory compliance exists to ensure.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Does a fouled hull affect underwater radiated noise?
retrieval_cards.answer: Yes, and significantly. Fouling roughens the blade and hull surfaces and disturbs the inflow to the propeller, which advances cavitation inception and makes the cavitation that does occur more unsteady. A fouled ship is both slower and louder, which is why hull and propeller condition is an acoustic measure and not only an efficiency one.
retrieval_cards.why: It links the maintenance limb to the physics limb and is the clearest example of the efficiency overlap.
